text: RTAB-Map (rtabmap_ros apt for Jazzy arm64) deployed on the server Pi 4b by Ansible: RGB-D + 2D scan inputs, publish_tf false, memory management tuned for the Pi 4b; inputs are compressed head RGB, ToF depth, camera_info, /scan_filtered, odometry and TF from the client.
Client-to-server transport proven over WiFi (DDS UDPv4; rates and sizes budgeted; client CPU cost of the extra streams measured).
The 3D map is aligned with slam_toolbox's map frame; save/load of the 3D map database alongside the 2D map.
Web UI: 3D map view (point cloud) in the existing map3d view, downsampled for the browser.
Agent: tools to query the 3D map (what is at a location, height of obstacles, free space around a point).
Tests, READMEs, Grafana CPU/memory checks on both Pis; deployed and verified by mapping a room.
RTAB-Map runs on the server Pi 4b, fed compressed head RGB + ToF depth + lidar over WiFi.
Web UI 3D map view in the existing map3d view.
Agent tools to query the 3D map.
Outdoor elevation mapping and 3D path planning are out of scope.

The lidar map should extend the ToF and 3D SLAM where possible. Interpretation: the 360 deg, ~12 m RPLidar complements the narrow 4 m ToF; RTAB-Map gets /scan_filtered with the RGB-D, and the 3D map view and queries show lidar-derived structure (2D-map walls extruded to a configurable height) where no depth has been seen, clearly distinguishable from measured 3D points, within the Pi 4b budget. Planned per D13: the lidar reaches the 3D map through slam_toolbox (RTAB-Map's odometry is slam_toolbox's lidar localisation; /map walls extruded in the web UI and reported as lidar_2d by the agent), because fusing scan into RTAB-Map's grid makes scan and depth points indistinguishable and scan links would break the D7 alignment.
